rv.q: And they have succeeded beyond any expectation I had prior to seeing it.
Henry Ong’s Ascent is a tempest in a Fabergé jewel box.
Whether or not you had the great good fortune of knowing Henry, his final play is a theatrical event worth celebrating.
I highly recommend for all to watch this play about this incredible man brought to life by such talented artists...
This is a very well-made production, but it raises the question of what this play could have been if the playwright, who passed away in 2018, had been able to sign off on the final draft.
But the revelation of Xuesen's fate so soon deflates a potential climax, especially since most Americans are not familiar with his story and wouldn't necessarily know what befell him.
It feels comprehensive in its stringing together of facts, but those facts are presented in a confusing jumble of exposition that frequently leave timeframe unclear.

cn.t: Ong's final play about deported Chinese rocket scientist Qian Xuesen offers a timely history lesson with strong performances, though critics find it doesn't fully realize its dramatic potential despite the compelling subject matter.
